🇺🇸🇮🇷🇮🇶 US strikes fail to break Iraq's resistance as it adopts Iran's fragmentation deterrence strategy
As the US increases pressure on Iraq to confront pro-Iranian armed groups, the resistance appears to be hardening its position and restructuring its operational approach, according to The Cradle.
🔶 On July 29, US and Saudi [forces carried out airstrikes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72849) against Popular Mobilization Units across seven Iraqi provinces, from Basra to Nineveh
🔶 The strikes were presented as retaliation for drone attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure that the US claimed had originated from Iraqi territory
🔶 However, no concrete evidence was provided to substantiate these allegations, and Iraqi authorities were not given advance notice of the operation. Iraq had requested intelligence and formed an investigative committee, but the airstrikes overtook the inquiry before it could reach any conclusion
🔴 The fragmentation strategy
The strikes have not led to capitulation or inflicted lasting damage on the resistance, which has already adapted to such pressure. New cells have emerged from within the resistance factions, formed by elements who left larger groups partly in opposition to proposed disarmament plans.
🔴 This fragmentation offers several strategic advantages:
🔴 A dispersed structure makes it significantly more difficult for adversaries to predict actions or dismantle the organization through targeted strikes against leadership or intelligence penetration
🔴 The decentralized command structure allows autonomous operations without waiting for orders from central leadership, complicating attribution and response
🔴 Destroying one group does not solve the problem—new formations emerge to fill the void
This is a proven Iranian tactic, refined during the war with the US. Iran's ["mosaic defense" doctrine](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65841) organizes defensive structures into multiple semi-independent regional layers instead of concentrating power in a single chain of command that could be paralyzed by a decapitation strike.
Under this model, if senior leaders are killed or communications are cut, local units still retain the authority and capacity to act. This approach was successfully employed to preserve military capabilities and strike US bases, and Iraqi factions are now adopting the same strategy for their own operations.
🔴 White House's leverage and its limits
The US wields significant economic leverage over Iraq through its dependence on oil revenues held at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. The Iraqi state budget is almost entirely financed by crude exports, which means the [US holds the country's economy hostage](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72019).
👉 However, the same pressure that works on the Iraqi government has not produced the intended result among the armed factions, who operate through informal networks and decentralized structures that are less vulnerable to financial coercion.
The US-Saudi strikes were meant to signal that attacks on Gulf targets would not be tolerated. Instead, they have accelerated the fragmentation of Iraq's resistance and obscured its chain of command, making future operations harder to attribute and deter. The resistance remains an important component of [the regional axis opposing US and Saudi influence](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73028) in the Middle East, and its ability to adapt and endure continues to pose a strategic challenge that America's current toolkit of airstrikes and financial pressure is not designed to resolve.

events.text:
🚨🇨🇳 China’s Unique Carrier Doctrine Uses Mainland to Counter U.S. Carrier Fleet
⚓️ China’s emerging carrier doctrine treats each ship as a mobile aviation node inside a much larger regional combat system. In the Western Pacific, land-based aircraft, missiles, satellites and sensors can perform functions that an American carrier group must carry at sea or obtain from overseas bases.
🇺🇸 The US Navy built its carrier force for expeditionary warfare thousands of kilometers from the continental United States. A strike group therefore brings its own fighters, early-warning aircraft, electronic warfare, air defenses, escorts and supply ships. Everything must fit aboard a limited number of hulls and remain connected across long maritime logistics lines.
🗺 China’s principal theaters—the Taiwan Strait, East and South China Seas and the approaches to the Western Pacific—lie beside its industrial and military heartland. Carriers operating there can remain connected to airfields, command centers, repair infrastructure and ammunition stocks on Chinese territory.
🚀 The supporting firepower extends far beyond the coastline. J-20 and J-16 fighters, H-6 missile-carrying bombers and land-based early-warning aircraft can reinforce the carrier air wing. The Rocket Force fields the DF-21D anti-ship ballistic missile with a range exceeding 1,500 km and the longer-range DF-26, while satellites and other sensors help track targets across the region.
🎯 These systems allow a Chinese carrier to concentrate on the missions where mobility matters most: moving stealth fighters and radar coverage beyond the coast, closing gaps between land-based aviation zones and establishing air and sea control on the Pacific side of Taiwan. The carrier is not required to generate the entire attack by itself.
🛫 Fujian gives this concept a substantially stronger mobile component. The 80,000-ton carrier’s electromagnetic catapults can launch J-35 stealth fighters, heavily loaded J-15T fighters, J-15DT electronic-warfare aircraft and the KJ-600 fixed-wing early-warning aircraft. Unlike the ski-jump systems on Liaoning and Shandong, catapults allow aircraft to take off with more fuel and weapons while supporting large specialized aircraft.
🧩 China’s Defense Ministry calls this combination of stealth fighter, multirole fighter, electronic-warfare aircraft, fixed-wing early warning and anti-submarine helicopter the carrier’s “five-piece set.” Its official purpose is to create the system-level combat capability of the entire formation, rather than merely adding more jets to one ship.
🔥 Around Taiwan, the carrier can operate east of the island while mainland missiles and aircraft cover the strait and place approaching US forces and regional bases under pressure. Pentagon reporting says China has already incorporated carriers into simulated blockade operations intended to complicate third-party intervention.
⚖️ China currently has three carriers against America’s 11, although the Pentagon expects the Chinese fleet to reach nine by 2035. That comparison understates the regional balance. In a Western Pacific conflict, the relevant equation is three Chinese flight decks backed by the PLA’s mainland missile, air and sensor network against US carriers operating inside the reach of that same network.

😲 Sharaa’s pipe dream bursts: Syria-Iraq oil pipeline will cost double, take until at least 2030 to build
 
The 2M bpd mega-energy link designed to give Iraq’s oil producers a Mediterranean alternative to Hormuz and provide Syria with much-needed transit fee income to rebuild its shattered economy has run into two new impediments: price and time.
Sources informed with the project told Reuters the project would cost “at least $15B.” That’s ~188-333% more than [the previously estimated $4.5-8B price tag. ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73269)
Hopes of rehabilitating the existing pipeline (long defunct and damaged during the 2003 US invasion of Iraq) are not feasible, with “entirely new infrastructure” required, the sources said. That means a construction timeframe of at least four years – possibly more to dismantle the old pipeline and resecure land rights in Syria.
👉 The new “integrated crude oil pipeline system” would also need to connect to southern Iraqi oil fields via a hub in Haditha, Anbar governorate, per demands from US oil giant Chevron, which is involved in the technical studies on the project, and looking to secure new oil rights in southern Iraq’s West Qurna 2 and Nassiriya fields.
US officials present the Syria-Iraq pipeline plan as a prospective alternative to Hormuz, with Treasury chief Bessent recently declaring that “the Strait is going to become irrelevant,” and claiming that 50-70% of its oil shipments will be passed on to pipelines over the next two years.
🛢 But Bessent’s math doesn’t add up. Diverting 10-14M bpd of oil from Hormuz to pipelines runs up against a shortfall of 5.3-9.3B bpd in pipeline capacity, not counting the fact that Saudi Arabia’s 7M bpd nominal capacity East-West pipeline with 2M bpd to spare is currently paralyzed by [the Houthis’ blockade on the Saudis’ Red Sea ports.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72694)
The UAE’s ADCOP Pipeline, another Hormuz workaround, has a 1.5M bpd capacity, with plans to more than double it to 3.6M bpd, but not before mid-2027 at the earliest.
As for the Syrian route, has Washington forgotten that the country’s been destroyed in a CIA dirty war and turned into a partially occupied failed state of roving terrorist gangs, disaffected Assad supporters, Kurdish forces and pro-Iranian militia neighbors?

🇮🇷🇺🇸 Iran’s ‘peace through strength’ doctrine leaves US military options looking thinner
Iran has taken a clear lesson from its past with the U.S.: when America speaks of peace, it helps to watch its bombers. 
So, according to the WSJ, Iran has spent the past two months building a layered deterrence strategy designed to make another US attack far harder to launch — and much harder to contain.
👉 Iran had reasons to be suspicious. In June 2025, Washington was publicly talking up diplomatic progress through mediators before joining Israeli strikes during the 12-day war. Then, in February 2026, US bombing began just two days after talks in Geneva.
So when a memorandum of understanding was signed in mid-June, Iran apparently decided that taking American assurances at face value would be a rather expensive habit.
Over the following two months:
🔶 The IRGC expanded its oversight of the regular army, elevated [commanders with battlefield experience](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73266) from the Iran-Iraq war to key posts, and stepped up domestic counterintelligence 
🔶 Production of missiles and drones was accelerated, while military advisers were dispatched to Iran-aligned groups in Iraq, Yemen, and Lebanon to[ prepare for joint operations ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73028)
🔶 Saudi Arabia found its oil exports more [exposed to attacks](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73490) from both Yemen and Iraq, and Gulf states received a stark warning not to interfere in the conflict
🔶 Iran also [struck Kurdish separatist groups](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73370) to guarantee their non-interference in the event of a potential US ground invasion.
By expanding its forces and creating multiple points of tension across the region, Iran has forced its counterparts to [stretch their resources](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73465) and raises the cost of escalation, compelling the US to reconsider a military solution to the conflict.

👏Staged drama for the goyim? Kushner said to grill Netanyahu for four hours on Gaza
The Trump son-in-law and Middle East policy point man met with Israel’s prime minister in Egypt on Sunday and demanded that Netanyahu “not create obstacles” to the implementation of the Gaza ceasefire plan, an Israeli source “familiar with the discussions” told CNN.
👹Netanyahu’s reaction? That it would be “problematic” to implement the plan ahead of Israel’s looming elections. Instead, Hamas should completely disarm first, according to Bibi – a complete non-starter for the Palestinian militant group.
👉Kushner and members of the Board of Peace also separately [met with a Hamas delegation](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73505), where specific mechanisms for disarmament, the transfer of power, Israeli withdrawal, humanitarian aid, and Israel’s ceasefire violations were discussed, with Kushner pressured to “compel” Israel to honor the US-brokered agreement.
👉Trump, for his part, said Monday that he “may endorse somebody” ahead of Israel’s looming vote, but will otherwise “stay out of Israeli elections.”
👉Kushner’s supposed hard line on Netanyahu echoes the back-and-forth, Days of Our Lives-style soap opera of public friction in the [Trump-Netanyahu relationship](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72864), which first began in 2020 after Bibi rushed to congratulate Biden in an election whose results Trump was contesting.

🗺 Kushner's Hamas talks: More empty Gaza diplomacy
President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner has held a rare meeting with Hamas leaders in Egypt, attempting to salvage a stalled ceasefire plan for Gaza. The talks came just days after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu publicly rejected the US-backed 15-point roadmap, which calls for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw from the flattened enclave.
Kushner's diplomatic efforts, however, have yielded little more than a string of failed projects and broken promises. He has spent months shuttling between Hamas and Israeli officials, but [the situation has barely shifted from its stalemate](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72935).
👍 Grand ambitions and dismal outcomes
Kushner's diplomatic role is less about achieving peace than about shaping perception. His once relentlessly touted $70–112 billion [Gaza "Riviera" redevelopment plan](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/61181) has been [reduced to a pilot project](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72346) involving portable cabins in Rafah. Yet even that modest scheme remains dead in the water with no cabins built, and the international security force intended to oversee it now a mere mirage. 
In Albania, Kushner's pattern of self-serving grandiosity is even more visible. He and Ivanka Trump are promoting a $4 billion luxury resort on the protected coast of one of Europe's poorest nations,[ sparking outrage and mass protests](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72831) among locals.
👹 No leverage over Israel
As a negotiator, Kushner appears to have no meaningful sway over Israel. Netanyahu has publicly rejected the US roadmap, and Israeli strikes on Gaza continue unabated.
The White House, nevertheless, has not withdrawn its support from the Israeli prime minister, viewing his actions as part of his election campaign strategy.
Kushner's meetings with Hamas leaders ultimately appear to be little more than a performance, designed to create the illusion of diplomatic activity while [Israel retains full freedom of action](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73274).
❗️Meanwhile, the situation in Gaza continues to deteriorate at an alarming pace:
🔴 Israel now occupies roughly 60 percent of the territory and has signaled its intention to expand control to 70 percent. Periodic ceasefire violations and airstrikes have killed and wounded dozens of Palestinians in recent days
🔴 Hospitals are running out of electricity and essential medications, including treatments for[ cancer patients](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73453). The enclave's 2 million residents face severe shortages of food, water, and medical supplies, with the UN warning of potential famine-like conditions in the north
🔴 Almost 90 percent of the population has been displaced, and reconstruction remains impossible as Israel continues to block the entry of construction materials and heavy equipment
